translations.text: The Lord called Moses and spoke to him from the tent of testimony, saying:
Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: If anyone among you presents an offering to the Lord from the livestock, you shall present your offerings from cattle or sheep.

If his offering is a burnt offering from the cattle, he shall present a male without blemish. He shall bring it to the entrance of the tent of testimony, so that it may be accepted from him to make atonement before the Lord.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the offering, so that it may be accepted for him to make atonement for himself.
They shall slaughter the young bull before the Lord, and the priests, Aaron’s sons, shall present the blood and pour it around the altar that stands at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
They shall skin the burnt offering and cut it up, limb by limb.
The priests, Aaron’s sons, shall put fire on the altar and pile wood on the fire.
The priests, Aaron’s sons, shall place the limbs, the head, and the fat on the wood that is on the fire upon the altar.
They shall wash the entrails and the legs with water, and the priests shall place everything on the altar, for it is a burnt offering, a sacrifice with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If the offering to the Lord is from the sheep, from lambs or young goats, as a burnt offering, he shall present a male without blemish.
He shall lay his hand on its head, and they shall slaughter it on the north side of the altar before the Lord. The priests, Aaron’s sons, shall pour its blood around the altar.
They shall cut it up, limb by limb, and the priests shall place these, together with its head and its fat, on the wood and the fire that are on the altar.
They shall wash the entrails and the legs with water, and the priest shall present everything and place it on the altar, for it is a burnt offering, a sacrifice with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If he presents an offering of birds to the Lord as a burnt offering, he shall bring his offering from turtledoves or pigeons.
The priest shall bring it to the altar and wring off its head. The priest shall place it on the altar and drain its blood at the base of the altar.
He shall remove the crop with its feathers and throw it beside the altar, at the place where the ashes are piled.

He shall split it at the wings but shall not separate it completely. The priest shall place it on the altar, on the wood and the fire, for it is a burnt offering, a sacrifice with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If anyone presents an offering to the Lord, his offering shall be fine flour. He shall pour oil over it and put frankincense on it, for it is a sacrifice.

He shall bring it to the priests, Aaron’s sons. He shall take a handful of the fine flour together with its oil and all its frankincense, and the priest shall place its memorial portion on the altar, a sacrifice with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
What remains of the sacrifice shall belong to Aaron and his sons. It is most holy among the sacrifices to the Lord.

If he presents an offering, a sacrifice baked in an oven, as an offering to the Lord, it shall consist of fine flour: unleavened loaves of fine flour mixed with oil and unleavened wafers spread with oil.
If your offering is a sacrifice prepared in a frying pan, it shall be fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened.
You shall break it into pieces and pour oil over them, for it is a sacrifice to the Lord.
If your offering is a sacrifice prepared on a griddle, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.
You shall present to the Lord the sacrifice that you make from these things and bring it to the priest. When the priest has brought it to the altar,
he shall take its memorial portion from the sacrifice, and the priest shall place it on the altar. It is an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Whatever remains of the offering shall belong to Aaron and his sons; it is most holy among your offerings.
You shall not make any offering that you present to the Lord with leaven. You shall not present anything leavened or anything containing honey as an offering to the Lord.
You may present these to the Lord as an offering of firstfruits, but they shall not go up on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Every offering you present shall be salted with the Lord’s salt. You shall not leave the salt of your God’s covenant out of your offerings; with every offering you shall present salt.
If you present an offering of the first grain to the Lord, you shall present fresh roasted grain, crushed and ground, to the Lord as an offering of your first grain.
You shall pour oil on it and put frankincense on it, for it is an offering.
The priest shall offer up its memorial portion, taken from the roasted grain with its oil, and all its frankincense, for it is an offering to the Lord.
If his offering to the Lord is a sacrifice of well-being, and he presents it from the cattle, whether male or female, he shall present an animal without blemish before the Lord.
He shall lay his hands on the head of the offering and slaughter it at the entrance of the tent of testimony. Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall pour its blood all around the altar of burnt offerings.
From the sacrifice of well-being he shall present an offering to the Lord: the fatty membrane covering the abdomen and all the fat of the entrails,
and the two kidneys and the fat on them near the loins. They shall remove the lobe of the liver together with the kidneys.
Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall offer it up on the altar as a burnt offering, upon the wood and the fire, as an offering of a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
If his offering is from the flock, as a sacrifice of well-being to the Lord, he shall present a male or female without blemish.
If he presents a lamb as his offering, he shall present it before the Lord,
and lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it at the entrance of the tent of testimony. Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall pour its blood all around the altar.

From the sacrifice of well-being they shall present an offering to the Lord: the fat and the entire tail, which he shall remove together with the backbone, and the fatty membrane covering the abdomen and all the fat of the entrails,
and the two kidneys and the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver, removed together with the kidneys.
The priest shall offer it up on the altar as a pleasing aroma, an offering to the Lord.
If his offering is from the goats, he shall present it before the Lord,
and lay his hand on its head. They shall slaughter it before the Lord at the entrance of the tent of testimony, and Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall pour its blood all around the altar.
They shall offer up from it an offering to the Lord: the fat, the membrane covering the abdomen, and all the fat of the entrails.
He shall remove the two kidneys and the fat on them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver together with the kidneys.
The priest shall offer it up on the altar as an offering of a pleasing aroma to the Lord. All the fat belongs to the Lord.
This is an everlasting law throughout your generations, wherever you dwell: you shall eat neither any fat nor any blood.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the Israelites and say: If anyone sins unintentionally before the Lord by doing any of the things that the Lord’s commandments forbid,
If the anointed high priest sins, causing the people to sin, he shall present to the Lord a young bull from the herd without blemish as a sin offering for the sin he has committed.
He shall bring the bull to the entrance of the tent of testimony before the Lord and lay his hands on the bull’s head before the Lord, and they shall slaughter the bull before the Lord.
And the anointed, consecrated priest shall take some of the bull’s blood in his hands and bring it into the tent of testimony.
And the priest shall dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of the blood seven times with his finger before the Lord, toward the veil of the sanctuary.

The priest shall put some of the bull’s blood on the horns of the altar of blended incense before the Lord, which is in the tent of testimony. He shall pour out all the rest of the bull’s blood at the base of the altar of burnt offerings, which stands at the entrance to the tent of testimony.
And he shall remove all the fat from the bull of the sin offering: the fat covering the entrails and all the fat on the entrails,
and the two kidneys and the fat on them near the loins; he shall also remove the lobe of the liver together with the kidneys,
just as these are removed from the bull of the sacrifice of well-being. And the priest shall offer them on the altar of burnt offerings.
And the bull’s hide and all its flesh, together with its head and legs, its entrails and dung—
they shall carry the whole bull outside the camp to a clean place where the ashes are poured out, and burn it with fire on wood. It shall be burned on the ash heap.

But if the whole congregation of the Israelites acts in ignorance unintentionally, and the matter escapes the congregation’s notice, and they do anything forbidden by any of the Lord’s commandments and become guilty,

and the sin they have committed becomes known to them, the congregation shall present an unblemished bull from the herd for a sin offering, and they shall bring it to the entrance of the tent of testimony.
And the elders of the congregation shall lay their hands on the bull’s head before the Lord, and they shall slaughter the bull before the Lord.
And the anointed priest shall bring some of the bull’s blood into the tent of testimony.
And the priest shall dip his finger in the bull’s blood and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord, facing the veil of the sanctuary.

And the priest shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of blended incense that stands before the Lord in the tent of testimony. And he shall pour out all the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offerings, which is at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
He shall remove all its fat and offer it on the altar.
And he shall do to the bull just as he did to the bull of the sin offering; he shall do the same to this one. And the priest shall make atonement for them, and their sins shall be forgiven.
And they shall carry the whole bull outside the camp and burn the bull just as they burned the first bull, for it is an offering for the sins of the congregation.
And if a ruler sins and does anything forbidden by the commandments of the Lord God, and unintentionally becomes guilty,
and the sin he has committed becomes known to him, he shall present as his offering an unblemished male goat from among the goats.
And he shall lay his hands on the goat’s head, and they shall slaughter it in the place where they slaughter the burnt offerings before the Lord, for it is a sin offering.

And the priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offerings. And he shall pour out all its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offerings.
And he shall offer all its fat on the altar, like the fat of the sacrifice of well-being. And the priest shall make atonement for him for his sins, and he shall be forgiven.
And if a person from among the people of the land sins unintentionally by doing anything forbidden by any of the Lord’s commandments and becomes guilty,
and the sins he has committed become known to him, he shall present as his offering an unblemished female goat for the sin he has committed.
And he shall lay his hands on its head, and they shall slaughter the female goat for the sin offering in the place where they slaughter the burnt offerings.
And the priest shall take some of its blood with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offerings. And he shall pour out all its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offerings.

And he shall remove all its fat, just as the fat is removed from the burnt offering of well-being. And the priest shall offer it on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the Lord. And the priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be forgiven.
And if he offers a sheep as his offering, he shall offer a female without blemish.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and they shall slaughter it in the place where they slaughter the burnt offerings.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offerings. He shall pour out all the rest of its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offerings.

He shall remove all its fat, just as the fat is removed from the sheep offered as a peace offering. The priest shall place it on the altar as a burnt offering to the Lord. The priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he shall be forgiven.
If a person sins by hearing the words of an oath while he is a witness, whether he has seen the matter or knows about it, and does not report it, he shall bear his sin.

If a person touches something unclean, whether a carcass, something torn by a wild beast, any unclean thing, the carcass of an unclean animal, or the carcass of an unclean creeping creature, and it escapes his notice, he becomes unclean and incurs guilt.
Or if someone touches human uncleanness, or any uncleanness that makes a person unclean upon contact, and it escapes his notice, but afterward he becomes aware of it, he incurs guilt.

If a person vows to do something evil or good, whatever a person may vow by an oath [?], and it is forgotten and hidden from his sight, but afterward he becomes aware of it, he becomes guilty of one of these things.
He shall confess the sin he has committed.

For the trespass he has committed against the Lord and the sin he has committed, he shall offer a female from the flock, a ewe or a female goat, as a sin offering. The priest shall make atonement for him for his sins, and his sins shall be forgiven.
But if he cannot afford a sheep, he shall offer for the sin he has committed two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one as a sin offering and one as a burnt offering.
He shall bring them to the priest, and the priest shall first bring in the one intended as the sin offering. The priest shall wring its head from its neck but shall not sever it.
He shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar and drain the remaining blood at the base of the altar, for it is a sin offering.
He shall make the second bird a burnt offering according to the prescribed rule. The priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he shall be forgiven.

If he cannot afford a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons, he shall bring as his offering for the sin he has committed a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. He shall not pour oil on it or put frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.
He shall bring it to the priest. The priest shall take a handful of it as its memorial portion and place it on the altar of burnt offerings to the Lord, for it is a sin offering.

The priest shall make atonement for him for the sin he has committed in any one of these matters, and he shall be forgiven. What remains shall belong to the priest, as with the offering of fine flour.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:

If a person goes astray and unintentionally sins in regard to the Lord's holy things, he shall offer to the Lord for his trespass a ram without blemish from the flock, valued at fifty shekels of silver according to the sanctuary shekel, for the trespass he has committed.

He shall repay what he has wrongfully taken from the holy things, add a fifth of its value to it, and give it to the priest. The priest shall make atonement for him with the ram offered for his trespass, and he shall be forgiven.
If a person sins and does any of the things forbidden by the Lord's commandments, even though he does not know it, he incurs guilt and shall bear his sin.

He shall bring to the priest a ram without blemish from the flock, valued in silver, as a trespass offering. The priest shall make atonement for him for the wrong he committed unknowingly, without realizing it, and he shall be forgiven.
For he has indeed committed a trespass before the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
If a person sins and utterly disregards the Lord's commandments, and lies to his neighbor concerning a deposit, concerning [?], or concerning something stolen, or harms his neighbor in any way—
And if he finds something lost and denies it, and swears falsely concerning any of the things a person may do and thereby sin,
then, when he sins and incurs guilt, he shall restore what he stole, or make good the harm he caused, or return the deposit entrusted to him, or the lost thing he found.
For anything about which he swore falsely, he shall repay the principal and add a fifth to it. He shall give it to its owner on the day when his guilt is established.
For his offenses he shall bring to the Lord an unblemished ram from the flock, valued in silver, for the offense he committed.
The priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord, and he shall be forgiven for any of the things he did by which he incurred guilt.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Command Aaron and his sons and say: This is the law of the burnt offering: it shall burn on the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar burning upon it shall not go out.
The priest shall put on a linen tunic and put linen trousers over his body. He shall remove the offerings of the burnt offering on the altar that the fire consumes, and place them beside the altar.
He shall take off his tunic and put on another tunic, and carry the burnt offering outside the camp to a clean place.
The fire burning on the altar must not go out. The priest shall burn wood on it every morning, place the burnt offering on it, and place the fat of the peace offerings on it.
The fire shall burn continually on the altar and shall not go out.
This is the law of the grain offering that Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall present before the Lord, in front of the altar.

He shall take a handful of the fine flour of the grain offering, together with its oil and the frankincense on the grain offering, and place it on the altar as an offering, a pleasing aroma, its memorial portion for the Lord.
Aaron and his sons shall eat what remains of it. It shall be eaten unleavened in a holy place; they shall eat it in the courtyard of the tabernacle of testimony.
It shall not be baked with leaven. I have given it to them as their portion from the offerings to the Lord. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
Every male among the priests shall eat it. This is a perpetual ordinance throughout your generations concerning the offerings to the Lord. Whatever touches them shall become holy.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:

This is the offering of Aaron and his sons that they shall present to the Lord on the day when you anoint him: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a continual grain offering, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.
It shall be prepared on a griddle, mixed with oil. He shall present it purified, as a grain offering in pieces, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
The priest from among his sons who is anointed in his place shall prepare it. This is a perpetual ordinance: it shall be offered entirely to the Lord.
Every grain offering of a priest shall be wholly burned and shall not be eaten.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:

Speak to Aaron and his sons and say: This is the law of the sin offering: in the place where they slaughter the burnt offering, they shall also slaughter the sin offering before the Lord. It is most holy.
The priest who presents it shall eat it. It shall be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the tabernacle of testimony.
Whatever touches its flesh shall become holy. Any garment on which some of its blood is sprinkled shall be washed in a holy place.
The earthenware vessel in which it is cooked shall be broken. If it is cooked in a bronze vessel, that vessel shall be scraped and rinsed with water.
Every male among the priests shall eat it. It is most holy to the Lord.
No sin offering whose blood is brought into the tabernacle of testimony to make atonement in the sanctuary shall be eaten; it shall instead be burned with fire.
This is the law of the ram offered for guilt, for it is most holy.
In the place where they slaughter the burnt offering, they shall also slaughter the ram for the guilt offering before the Lord, and he shall pour its blood around the base of the altar.
He shall remove all its fat: the fat tail, all the fat covering the entrails, and all the fat on the entrails.
He shall remove both kidneys and the fat over them near the loins, and the lobe of the liver together with the kidneys.
The priest shall offer these on the altar as an offering to the Lord, for it is a guilt offering.
Every male among the priests may eat it. They shall eat it in a holy place, for it is most holy.
The guilt offering is like the sin offering: one and the same law shall apply to them. It shall belong to the priest who makes atonement with it.
The priest who offers anyone’s burnt offering shall receive the hide of the burnt offering that he offers.
Every grain offering prepared in an oven, and every offering prepared on a griddle or in a pan, shall belong to the priest who offers it.
Every grain offering mixed with oil, and every one not mixed with oil, shall belong equally to all the sons of Aaron, each sharing alike.
This is the law of the peace offerings that they offer to the Lord.

If he offers it for thanksgiving, he shall offer with the thanksgiving sacrifice unleavened loaves of fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and fine flour mixed with oil in flat cakes.
He shall present his offering with unleavened bread along with his thanksgiving peace offering.
From all his offerings he shall present one of each as a contribution to the Lord. It shall belong to the priest who pours out the blood of the peace offering.
The meat of his thanksgiving peace offering shall be his. It shall be eaten on the day it is offered, and they shall leave none of it until morning.
If someone voluntarily presents his offering as a vow, it shall be eaten on the day he offers the sacrifice, and also on the following day.
Whatever remains of the meat of the sacrifice until the third day shall be burned with fire.

If any of the meat of his peace offering is eaten on the third day, it shall not be acceptable to the one who offered it, nor shall it be credited to him, for it is something accursed and unclean. Anyone who eats any of it shall bear guilt.
Meat that touches anything unclean shall not be eaten but shall be burned with fire. Anyone who is clean may eat the meat.
Anyone who eats from the peace offering that belongs to the Lord while uncleanness is upon him shall be cut off from his people.

Anyone who touches anything unclean—human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean, detestable thing—and then eats the meat of the peace offering that belongs to the Lord shall be cut off from his people.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the Israelites and say: You shall not eat any fat of cattle, sheep, or goats.
The fat of animals that die on their own or are torn by wild beasts may be used for any purpose, but it shall not be eaten as food.
Anyone who eats the fat of animals from which you present an offering to the Lord shall be cut off from his people.
You shall not eat any blood, whether from birds or from any animals, in any of your dwellings.
Anyone who eats blood shall be cut off from his people.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the Israelites and say: Whoever presents a peace offering to the Lord shall bring his offering to the Lord from his peace sacrifice.
His own hands shall present the offering to the Lord. He shall bring the fat of the breast and the lobe of the liver to place before the Lord.
The priest shall offer it up on the altar, and the breast shall belong to Aaron and his sons.
You shall give the right shoulder to the priest as his portion from your peace offerings.
The one among Aaron’s sons who offers the blood of the peace offering and the fat shall have the right shoulder as his portion.

For I have taken the breast of the presentation offering and the shoulder of the dedicated offering from the Israelites, from your peace offerings, and have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as a perpetual statute for the Israelites.
This is the anointing portion of Aaron and his sons from the offerings to the Lord, on the day when he presented them.
As the Lord commanded, the Israelites shall give it to them on the day when he anointed them, as a perpetual statute throughout their generations.
This is the law for burnt offerings and sacrifices, for sin offerings and guilt offerings, for ordination and for peace offerings,
as the Lord commanded Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day when the Lord commanded the Israelites to present their offerings before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Take Aaron and his sons, their robes, the anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread.
Gather all the people at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
Moses did as the Lord commanded him and gathered the people at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
Moses said to the people, “This is what the Lord commanded to be done.”
Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
He clothed Aaron in the tunic, fastened the sash around his waist, put the robe on him, and placed the ephod on him. He bound it to him with the woven band of the ephod and secured it on him.
He placed the breastpiece on him and put the Revelation and the Truth on the breastpiece.
He placed the turban on his head, and on the front of the turban he placed the gold plate, consecrated and holy, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Moses took some of the anointing oil and sprinkled it on the altar seven times.
He anointed the altar and consecrated it, along with all its utensils, the basin, and its base, and consecrated them. He anointed the tabernacle and everything in it and consecrated it.
Moses poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head, anointed him, and consecrated him.
Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, clothed them in robes, put sashes around their waists, and placed turbans on them, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Moses brought forward the bull for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the bull for the sin offering.

He slaughtered it, and Moses took some of its blood and put it with his finger on the horns all around the altar, purifying the altar. He poured out the blood at the base of the altar and consecrated it to make atonement upon it.
He took all the fat of the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys, and all the fat on them, and Moses offered them up on the altar.
He burned the bull, its hide, its flesh, and its dung with fire outside the camp, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Moses brought forward the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
Moses slaughtered the ram and poured its blood around the altar.
He cut the ram into pieces, limb by limb, and Moses took the head, the pieces, and the fat.

He washed the entrails and the legs with water, and Moses offered up the whole ram on the altar as a burnt offering with a pleasing aroma, for it is an offering to the Lord, as the Lord commanded Moses.
Moses brought forward the second ram, the ram of ordination, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram’s head.
And he slaughtered it, and Moses took some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron’s right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.

And Moses brought Aaron’s sons forward, and Moses put some of the blood on the lobes of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. And Moses poured the blood all around the altar.
And he took the fat, the rump, the fat covering the entrails, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys and the fat covering them, and the right thigh.
And from the basket of ordination offerings that stood before the Lord, he took one unleavened loaf and one loaf made with oil, and placed them on the fat and on the right thigh.
And he placed everything in Aaron’s hands and in the hands of his sons, and presented it as an offering before the Lord.
And Moses took it from their hands and offered it on the altar as a burnt offering of ordination, a pleasing aroma, an offering to the Lord, as the Lord had commanded.
And Moses took the breast and raised it as an offering before the Lord. It was from the ram of ordination and became Moses’ portion, as the Lord had commanded Moses.

And Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood on the altar and sprinkled Aaron and his garments, his sons and their garments. And he consecrated Aaron and his garments, and his sons and his sons’ garments with him.

And Moses said to Aaron and his sons, “Boil the meat in the courtyard of the Tent of Testimony, in a holy place, and eat it there with the loaves that are in the basket of ordination offerings, as the Lord commanded me, saying, ‘Aaron and his sons shall eat it.’
“And burn the remaining bread and meat with fire.
“And do not go out from the entrance of the Tent of Testimony for seven days, until the day when the days of your ordination are completed, for your ordination will take seven days.
“As was done on that day, so the Lord commanded it to be done to make atonement for you.
“And remain at the entrance of the Tent of Testimony for seven days, night and day, and keep the Lord’s charge so that you do not die, for this is what the Lord commanded me.”
And Aaron and his sons did everything that the Lord had commanded Moses.
And on the eighth day, Moses called Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel.
And Moses said to Aaron, “Take for yourself a calf from the herd for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering, both without blemish, and present them before the Lord.
“And speak to the elders of Israel and say, ‘Take for yourselves a male goat for a sin offering, and a ram, a calf, and a year-old lamb, without blemish, for a burnt offering,
“‘and a calf and a ram for a burnt offering of well-being before the Lord, and an offering of fine flour mixed with oil, for today the Lord will appear among you.’”
And they brought what Moses had commanded before the Tent of Testimony, and the whole congregation approached and stood before the Lord.
And Moses said, “This is what the Lord said to do, and the glory of the Lord will appear to you.”

And Moses said to Aaron, “Approach the altar and offer your sin offering and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and your household. And offer the sacrifices of your people and make atonement for them, as the Lord commanded Moses.”
And Aaron approached the altar and slaughtered the calf that was his sin offering.
And Aaron’s sons brought the blood to him, and he dipped his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the altar, and poured the blood at the base of the altar.
And he offered the fat, the kidneys, and the lobe of the liver from the sin offering on the altar, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And they burned the meat and the hide with fire outside the camp.
He slaughtered the burnt offering, and Aaron’s sons brought him the blood, and he poured it around the altar.
They brought him the burnt offering piece by piece, along with the head, and he placed them on the altar.
He washed the entrails and the legs with water and placed them on top of the burnt offering on the altar.
They brought the people’s offering. He took the goat for the people’s sin offering and slaughtered it as he had the first one.
He brought the burnt offering and offered it as prescribed.
He brought the grain offering, filled his hands with some of it, and placed it on the altar, in addition to the morning burnt offering.
He slaughtered the bull and the ram as the people’s peace offering. Aaron’s sons brought him the blood, and he poured it around the altar.
And the fat from the bull and the ram, the rump, the fatty covering of the entrails, the two kidneys with their fat, and the lobe of the liver—
they placed the fat on the breasts and brought up the fat together with the breasts, and placed the fat on the altar.
He presented the breasts and the right thigh as an offering before the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Aaron raised his hands over the people and blessed them. He came down after offering the sin offering, the burnt offerings, and the peace offering.
Moses and Aaron entered the tent of testimony. When they came out, they blessed all the people, and the glory of the Lord appeared to all the people.
Fire came out from the Lord and consumed what was on the altar—the burnt offering and the fat. All the people saw it and were terrified, and they fell on their faces.
Aaron’s two sons, Nadab and Abihu, each took his censer, put fire in them, added incense, and presented unauthorized fire before the Lord, which the Lord had not commanded them to offer.
Fire came out from the Lord and consumed them, and they died before the Lord.
Moses said to Aaron, “This is what the Lord said: ‘Among those who draw near to me I will be shown holy, and before all my people I will be glorified.’” And Aaron was deeply shaken.
Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, Aaron’s uncle, and said to them, “Come forward and carry your brothers, with their tunics, away from the sanctuary to outside the camp.”
They came forward and carried them, with their tunics, outside the camp, just as Moses had said.

Moses said to Aaron and to his surviving sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, “Do not uncover your heads or tear your clothes, so that you do not die and wrath does not come upon the people. But let your brothers and the whole house of Israel mourn for those who were burned by the Lord.
Do not leave the entrance of the tent of testimony, so that you do not die, for the anointing oil from the Lord is upon you.” And they did as Moses had said.
The Lord spoke to Aaron and said:

“Do not drink wine or strong drink, you or your sons with you, when you enter the tent of testimony or when you approach the altar, so that you do not die. This is a lasting law throughout your generations,
to distinguish between the holy and the profane, and between the clean and the unclean,
and to teach the Israelites all the laws that the Lord spoke to them through Moses.”
Moses said to Aaron and to his surviving sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, “Take the grain offering that remains from the offerings to the Lord, and eat it unleavened before the altar, for it is most holy.
Eat it in a holy place, for it is your allotted portion and your sons’ allotted portion from the offerings to the Lord. This is what I have been commanded.

And eat the breast of the offering and the thigh of the allotted portion in a holy place, you and your sons and your household with you, for it is your allotted portion and has been given as your sons’ allotted portion from the Israelites’ peace offerings.

They shall bring the shoulder of the contribution and the breast of the dedicated offering together with the offerings of fat, to present them as a dedicated offering before the Lord. They shall belong to you and to your sons and daughters with you, as a perpetual statute, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
Moses diligently searched for the goat of the sin offering, but it had been burned. Moses was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s surviving sons, and said:
“Why did you not eat the sin offering in a holy place? It is most holy, and he gave it to you to eat so that you might bear the sins of the people and make atonement for them before the Lord.
Its blood was not brought inside the sanctuary before him. You should therefore have eaten it in a holy place, just as I was commanded.”

Aaron spoke to Moses and said, “Even though today they presented their sin offering and their burnt offerings before the Lord, such things have happened to me. If I were to eat the sin offering today, perhaps it would not be pleasing before the Lord.”
Moses heard this, and it seemed acceptable to him.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said:
Speak to the children of Israel and say: “These are the animals you may eat among all the animals on the earth.
You may eat any animal that has split hooves, with its hooves divided in two, and chews the cud.
But among those that chew the cud and do not have split hooves, you must not eat the camel, because it chews the cud but its hoof is not divided. It shall be unclean for you.
And the hare, because it chews the cud but its foot is not divided, shall be unclean for you.
And the rabbit, because it chews the cud but its foot is not divided, shall be unclean for you.
And the pig, because it has split feet and hooves but does not chew the cud, shall be unclean for you.
You must not eat their flesh or touch their carcasses, because they shall be unclean for you.
These are what you may eat among all creatures in the waters: you may eat all those that have fins and scales in the waters, in the seas and in the streams.

You must not eat any that have no fins and scales in the waters, in the seas and in the streams, among everything the waters bring forth and among every living creature in the waters, because they are unclean. They shall be unclean for you.
You must not eat their flesh, and you must detest their dead bodies.
For everything in the waters that has no fins and scales shall be unclean for you.
These are the birds you must detest and must not eat, for they shall be unclean for you: the eagle, the griffon vulture, and the sea eagle;
and the vulture, the kite, and anything like them;
and the raven and anything like it;
and the ostrich, the owl, the gull, and anything like them, and the hawk and anything like it;
and the nightjar, the kestrel, and the ibis;
and the nightingale, the pelican, and the swan;
and the stork, the plover, and anything like them, and the hoopoe and the bat.
Every winged creeping creature that walks on four legs shall be unclean for you.
But among the winged insects that walk on all fours, you may eat those that have jointed legs above their feet with which to leap from the ground.
These are the ones you may eat: the [?] and anything like it, the [?] and anything like it, the locust and anything like it, and the snake-fighting insect and anything like it.
Every winged insect that has four feet shall be unclean for you.
Do not become unclean through them. Anyone who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
Anyone who carries their carcasses shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening.
Among all animals, those that have split hooves and spread their claws but do not chew the cud shall be unclean for you. Anyone who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
Everything that walks on its paws among all the beasts that walk on all fours shall be unclean for you. Anyone who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.
Anyone who carries any part of their carcasses shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening, for all these shall be unclean for you.
These shall be unclean for you among all the creeping creatures that creep on the earth: the weasel, the mouse, and the tortoise of every kind,
and the shrew, the chameleon, the gecko, the lizard, and the mole.
All these shall be unclean for you among all the creeping creatures that creep on the earth. Anyone who touches their carcasses shall be unclean until evening.

Anything on which any part of their carcasses falls shall be unclean, whether a wooden vessel, clothing, leather, or sackcloth—any article used for any work. It shall be immersed in water and remain unclean until evening; then it shall be clean.
If any of them falls into an earthenware vessel, everything inside it shall be unclean, and you shall break the vessel.
Any food that is eaten, on which any of that water falls, shall be unclean, and any drink that is drunk from any vessel shall be unclean.
Anything on which any part of their carcasses falls shall be unclean. Ovens and cooking hearths shall be demolished, because they have become unclean and shall be unclean for you.
But springs of water, wells, and pools of water shall remain clean for you. Anyone who touches their unclean carcasses shall be unclean.
But if any part of their carcasses falls on seed intended for sowing, it shall remain clean.
But if water has been poured on any seed and any part of their carcasses falls on it, it shall be unclean for you.
If any animal that you are allowed to eat dies, anyone who touches its carcass shall be unclean until evening.
Anyone who carries any part of its carcass shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening.
Every creeping creature that creeps on the earth shall be unclean for you and shall not be eaten.
You shall not eat anything that crawls on its belly, anything that walks on all fours, or anything with many feet, among all the creatures that move about on the earth, for these are unclean for you.
Do not make yourselves detestable through any creeping creatures that creep on the earth. Do not defile yourselves through them or become unclean through them.
I am the Lord your God. Sanctify yourselves and be holy, for I, the Lord your God, am holy. Do not defile yourselves through any creatures that move about on the earth.
For I am the Lord God who brought you out of the land of the Egyptians to be your God. Be holy, for I am holy.
This shall be the law concerning animals, birds, every living creature that moves in the water, and every living creature that moves on the earth.
to distinguish between the holy and the unholy, and to instruct the Israelites about the living creatures that may be eaten and the animals that may not be eaten.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:

Speak to the Israelites and say to them: If a woman conceives and gives birth to a male child, she shall be unclean for seven days; she shall be unclean as during the days of separation for her menstrual period.
On the eighth day, the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.
She shall remain thirty-three days in the purification of her blood. She shall not touch anything holy or enter the sanctuary until the days of her purification are completed.
But if she gives birth to a female child, she shall be unclean for seven days, as during her menstrual period, and shall remain sixty-six days in the purification of her blood.

When the days of her purification for a son or a daughter are completed, she shall bring a year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a pair of pigeons or turtledoves for a sin offering to the priest at the entrance of the tent of testimony.

The priest shall present it before the Lord and make atonement for her, and shall cleanse her from the source of her bleeding. This shall be the law for a woman who gives birth to a male or a female child.

But if she cannot afford a lamb, she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering. The priest shall make atonement for her, and she shall be clean.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said:

If someone has a scar, a swelling, or a bright spot on the skin of his body, and it becomes a leprous lesion on the skin of his body, he shall come to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who are priests.

The priest shall examine the lesion on the skin of his body. If the hair in the lesion has turned white and the lesion appears deeper than the skin of his body, it is a leprous lesion. The priest shall examine him and declare him unclean.

But if the bright spot on the skin of his body is white, does not appear deeper than the skin, and its hair has not turned white, and the spot itself is pale, the priest shall isolate the person with the lesion for seven days.
The priest shall examine him on the seventh day. If the lesion appears to him to be unchanged and has not changed in the skin, the priest shall isolate him for another seven days.

The priest shall examine him again on the seventh day. If the lesion is paler and has not changed its appearance in the skin, the priest shall declare him clean, for it is only a mark. He shall wash his clothes and be clean.
But if the mark spreads in the skin after the priest has examined him and declared him clean, he shall appear before the priest again.
The priest shall examine him, and if the mark has changed color in the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean, for it is leprosy.
If someone has a leprous lesion, he shall come to Aaron the priest.
The priest shall examine him. If there is a white swelling in the skin, its hair has turned white, and there is healthy, living flesh in the swelling,
it is longstanding leprosy in the skin of his body. The priest shall declare him unclean and isolate him, for he is unclean.
But if the leprosy spreads throughout the skin and covers all the skin of the body from head to foot, wherever the priest can see,
the priest shall examine him. If the leprosy has covered all the skin of his body, the priest shall declare the person with the lesion clean, because it has all turned white; he is clean.
But on the day when living flesh appears on him, he shall become unclean.
The priest shall examine the living flesh and declare the healthy flesh unclean. He shall be unclean, because it is leprosy.
But if the healthy flesh is restored again and turns white, he shall come to the priest.
The priest shall examine him. If his lesion has turned white, the priest shall declare the person with the lesion clean, because he is clean.
If a person has a boil on his skin and it heals,
and in the place of the boil there is a white, bright spot, pale or reddish, he shall show himself to the priest.
The priest shall examine it, and if it appears deeper than the skin and the hair has turned white, the priest shall declare him unclean, because leprosy has broken out in the boil.
But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in it, and it is not deeper than the skin but is faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
If it spreads over the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean, because a leprous lesion has broken out in the boil.
But if the bright spot remains in the same place and does not spread, it is the scar of the boil. The priest shall declare him clean.
If a person has a burn from fire on his skin, and his skin has healed from the burn, and the place of the burn is bright or glistening white or reddish or pale,

the priest shall examine him. If the hair in the bright spot has turned white and it appears lower than the skin, leprosy has broken out in the burn. The priest shall declare him unclean, because it is a leprous lesion.
If the priest examines it and there is no bright spot or white hair in it, and it is not lower than the skin but is faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
The priest shall examine him on the seventh day. If it has spread over the skin, the priest shall declare him unclean, for it is a lesion of leprosy that has broken out in the sore.
If the bright spot remains in the same place and does not spread over the skin, and it is faded, it is the scar of the burn. The priest shall declare him clean, because it is the mark of the burn.
If a man or woman has a leprous lesion on the head or in the beard,

the priest shall examine the lesion. If it appears lower than the skin and there is fine yellow hair in it, the priest shall declare him unclean, because it is a scaly infection. It is leprosy of the head or leprosy of the beard.
If the priest examines the scaly lesion and it does not appear lower than the skin, and there is no yellow hair in it, the priest shall isolate the scaly lesion for seven days.

The priest shall examine the lesion on the seventh day. If the scaly infection has not spread over the skin, and there is no yellow hair in it, and the scaly infection does not appear lower than the skin,
he shall shave him, but he shall not shave the infected area. The priest shall isolate the lesion for another seven days.

The priest shall examine the lesion on the seventh day. If the scaly infection has not spread over the skin after he was shaved, and the scaly infection does not appear lower than the skin, the priest shall declare him clean. He shall wash his clothes and be clean.
But if the scaly infection spreads over the skin after he was shaved,
the priest shall examine him. If the scaly infection has spread over the skin, the priest shall not look for yellow hair, because he is unclean.
But if the scaly infection remains in its place and dark hair grows in it, the scaly infection has healed. He is clean, and the priest shall declare him clean.
If a man or woman has a bright, shining, whitish spot on the skin of the body,
The priest shall examine him. If there is a pale, shining bright spot on the skin of his body, it is a scaly patch that has spread over the skin of his body. He is clean.
If someone's head loses its hair, he is bald; he is clean.
If his head loses its hair at the front, he is bald at the forehead; he is clean.
But if there is a white or reddish lesion on his bald head or bald forehead, it is leprosy hidden in his bald head or bald forehead.
The priest shall examine it. If the lesion on his bald head or bald forehead appears white or reddish, like the appearance of leprosy on the skin of his body,
he is a leprous man; he is unclean. The priest shall certainly declare him unclean, because his lesion is on his head.
The leprous person who has the lesion shall have his clothes torn and his head uncovered. He shall cover his mouth and shall be called unclean.
For as long as the lesion is on him, he shall be unclean; he is unclean. He shall live apart, and his dwelling shall be outside the camp.
If a garment has a leprous lesion, whether it is a woolen garment or a linen garment,
whether in the warp or in the weft, whether in linen or in wool, whether in a hide or in any article made of leather,
and the lesion is greenish or reddish in the hide or the garment, in the warp or the weft, in any article made of hide, or in any utensil, it is a leprous lesion, and he shall show it to the priest.
The priest shall examine the lesion, and the priest shall isolate the affected article for seven days.

The priest shall examine the lesion on the seventh day. If the lesion has spread through the garment, the warp or the weft, the linen or the wool, or the hide, whatever use the hide is put to, the lesion is persistent leprosy; it is unclean.
He shall burn the garment, whether the warp or the weft, of wool or linen, or any leather material in which the lesion is found, for it is persistent leprosy. It shall be burned with fire.
But if the priest examines it and the lesion has not spread through the garment, the warp or the weft, the wool or the linen, or any leather article,
the priest shall give orders that the affected article be washed, and the priest shall isolate it for seven days a second time.

The priest shall examine the lesion after it has been washed. If the appearance of the lesion has not changed, even though the lesion has not spread, it is unclean. It shall be burned with fire, for it is embedded in the garment, the warp, or the weft.
If the priest examines it and the lesion is paler after it has been washed, he shall tear that part out of the garment, the hide, the warp, or the weft.
But if it appears again in the garment, the warp or the weft, or any leather article, it is leprosy breaking out. The article in which the lesion is found shall be burned with fire.
Whether it is a garment, the warp or the weft, or any leather article that has been washed and from which the lesion has disappeared, it shall be washed a second time and shall be clean.
This shall be the law concerning a leprous lesion in a woolen or linen garment, in the warp or the weft, or in any leather article, for declaring it clean or unclean.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
This shall be the law for a leper on the day of his cleansing: he shall be brought to the priest.
The priest shall go outside the camp and examine him. If the lesion of leprosy has healed in the leper,
The priest shall give orders that two live, clean birds, fir wood, scarlet thread, and hyssop be taken for the person being cleansed.
The priest shall give orders that one bird be killed in an earthenware vessel over running water.
He shall take the live bird, the fir wood, the scarlet thread, and the hyssop, and dip them, together with the live bird, in the blood of the bird killed over the running water.
He shall sprinkle the person being cleansed from leprosy seven times, declare him clean, and release the live bird into the open field.

The person being cleansed shall wash his clothes, shave off all his hair, and wash himself with water, and he shall be clean. After that he shall enter the camp, but he shall remain outside his own house for seven days.

On the seventh day he shall shave off all his hair: the hair of his head, his beard, and his eyebrows. He shall shave off all his hair, wash his clothes, and wash his body with water, and he shall be clean.
On the eighth day he shall take two unblemished year-old male lambs, one unblemished year-old ewe lamb, three tenths of a measure of fine flour mixed with oil for an offering, and one cup of oil.
The priest who performs the cleansing shall place the man being cleansed, together with those things, before the tent of testimony.
The priest shall take one male lamb and present it as a guilt offering, together with the cup of oil, and present it as an offering before the Lord.

He shall slaughter the other lamb in the holy place where they slaughter the burnt offering and the sin offering. For the guilt offering, like the sin offering, shall belong to the priest; it is most holy.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest shall take some of the measure of oil and pour it into the priest’s left hand.
The priest shall dip his right finger into the oil in his left hand and sprinkle it with his finger seven times before the Lord.

The priest shall put the oil remaining in his hand on the lobe of the right ear of the person to be cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, in the place where the blood of the guilt offering was put.
The priest shall put the oil remaining in the priest’s hand on the head of the person being cleansed, and the priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord.
The priest shall offer the sin offering and make atonement for the person being cleansed from his sins. Then the priest shall slaughter the burnt offering.
The priest shall offer up the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar before the Lord. The priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be clean.

If he is poor and cannot afford this, he shall take one lamb as a guilt offering for the offense he committed, as an offering to make atonement for him, a tenth of a measure of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, and one measure of oil,
and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whichever he can afford. One shall be a sin offering and the other a burnt offering.
On the eighth day he shall bring these to the priest for his cleansing, to the entrance of the tent of testimony, before the Lord.
The priest shall take the lamb for the guilt offering and the measure of oil and present them as an offering before the Lord.

He shall slaughter the lamb for the guilt offering. The priest shall take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest shall pour some of the oil into the priest’s left hand.
With his right finger, the priest shall sprinkle some of the oil in his left hand seven times before the Lord.

The priest shall put some of the oil in his hand on the lobe of the right ear of the person being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot, in the place where the blood of the guilt offering was put.
He shall pour the oil remaining in the priest’s hand on the head of the person being cleansed, and the priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord.
He shall offer one of the turtledoves or young pigeons, according to what he can afford,
one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, together with the grain offering. The priest shall make atonement for the person being cleansed before the Lord.
This shall be the law for anyone who has a leprous infection and cannot afford what is required for his cleansing.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said:
When you enter the land of the Canaanites, which I give you as a possession, and I put a leprous infection in a house in the land you possess,
the owner of the house shall come and tell the priest, saying, ‘Something like an infection has appeared in my house.’
The priest shall order the house to be emptied before the priest enters to inspect the house, so that nothing in the house becomes unclean. Then the priest shall enter to examine the house.
The priest shall inspect the infection on the walls of the house: green or reddish depressions that appear lower than the surface of the walls.
The priest shall go out of the house to its entrance, and the priest shall shut up the house for seven days.
The priest shall return on the seventh day and inspect the house to see whether the infection has spread over the walls of the house.
The priest shall give orders to remove the stones on which the lesion appears and take them outside the city to an unclean place.
They shall scrape the entire inside of the house and dump the scrapings outside the city in an unclean place.
They shall take other dressed stones and put them in place of those stones, and they shall take other earth and plaster the house.
If the infestation returns and appears in the house after the stones have been removed, the house scraped, and plaster applied again,
the priest shall enter and inspect it. If the infestation has spread through the house, it is persistent leprosy in the house; it is unclean.
They shall tear down the house, its timber, its stones, and all the earth of the house, and take them outside the city to an unclean place.
Anyone who enters the house during any of the days when it is shut off shall be unclean until evening.
Anyone who sleeps in that house shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening, and anyone who eats in the house shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening.

If the priest comes in and inspects it, and the infestation has not spread through the house after the house was plastered, the priest shall declare the house clean, because the infestation has healed.
To cleanse the house, he shall take two living, clean birds, fir wood, spun scarlet thread, and hyssop.
He shall kill one bird in an earthenware vessel over running water.

He shall take the fir wood, the spun scarlet thread, the hyssop, and the living bird, and dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and in the running water, and sprinkle the house with them seven times.
He shall cleanse the house with the bird’s blood, the running water, the living bird, the fir wood, the hyssop, and the spun scarlet thread.
He shall release the living bird outside the city into the open country and make atonement for the house, and it shall be purified and be clean.
This shall be the law concerning every infestation of leprosy and every lesion,
and leprosy in clothing and in a house,
and a scar, a swelling, and a shiny spot,
to indicate on which day it is unclean and on which day it is clean. This shall be the law concerning leprosy.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said:
Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: Any man who has a discharge from his body—his discharge is unclean.

This shall be the law concerning his purity: if semen flows from his body, or if his flesh wastes away from the discharge, his uncleanness is in him throughout all the days of the discharge from his body. If his flesh wastes away because of the discharge, that is uncleanness of the body.
Every bed on which the man with a seminal discharge sleeps shall be unclean, and everything on which he sits shall be unclean.
Anyone who touches his bed shall rinse his clothes, wash himself with water, and be unclean until evening.
Anyone who sits on an object on which the man with a seminal discharge has sat shall rinse his clothes, wash himself with water, and be unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches the body of the man with a seminal discharge shall rinse his clothes, wash himself with water, and be unclean until evening.
If the saliva of the man with a seminal discharge gets on a clean person, that person shall rinse his clothes, wash himself with water, and be unclean until evening.
Every donkey saddle on which a man with a discharge sits shall be unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches anything that was underneath him shall be unclean until evening.
Anyone whom the man with a seminal discharge touches without having washed his hands with water shall rinse his clothes, wash his body with water, and be unclean until evening.
An earthenware vessel that the man with a discharge touches shall be broken, and every wooden vessel shall be washed with water and shall be clean.
If the man with a discharge becomes clean from his discharge, he shall count seven days for his cleansing, wash his clothes, and bathe his body in fresh running water, and he shall be clean.
On the eighth day he shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them before the Lord to the entrance of the tent of testimony, and give them to the priest.
The priest shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and the priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord for his discharge.
If a man has an emission of semen, he shall bathe his whole body in water and shall be unclean until evening.
Every garment and hide on which semen falls shall be washed with water and shall be unclean until evening.
If a man lies with a woman and emits semen, they shall bathe in water and shall be unclean until evening.
If a woman has a discharge of blood, and the discharge of blood is from her body, she shall remain in her menstruation for seven days. Everyone who touches her shall be unclean until evening.
Everything on which she lies during her menstruation, and everything on which she sits, shall be unclean.
Everyone who touches her bed shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and shall be unclean until evening.
Everyone who touches any object on which she sits shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and shall be unclean until evening.
If she is still in her bed or on any object on which she has sat, anyone who touches her shall be unclean until evening.
If a man lies with her and her uncleanness comes upon him, he shall be unclean for seven days, and every bed on which he lies shall be unclean until evening.

If a woman has a discharge of blood for many days outside the time of her menstruation, or if she has a discharge after her menstruation, all the days of her unclean discharge shall be like the days of her menstruation, and she shall be unclean.

Every bed on which she lies throughout the days of her discharge shall be unclean like the bed of her menstruation, and every object on which she sits shall be unclean, like the uncleanness of the days of her menstruation.
Everyone who touches her shall be unclean and shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and shall be unclean until evening.
But if she becomes clean from her discharge, she shall count seven days for herself, and afterward she shall be clean.
On the eighth day she shall take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
The priest shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and the priest shall make atonement for her before the Lord for her unclean discharge.
You shall keep the Israelites carefully away from their uncleanness, so that they do not die because of their uncleanness by defiling my tent, which is among them.
This shall be the law for a person with a discharge, and for anyone who has an emission of semen and becomes unclean through it,
and for a woman during her menstruation, and for anyone with a discharge, male or female, and for a man who lies with a menstruating woman.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said, after the death of Aaron’s sons, when they offered foreign fire before the Lord and perished:

And the Lord said to Moses, “Speak to Aaron your brother: they must not enter the sanctuary at any time behind the curtain, before the mercy seat that is on the ark of the testimony, lest he die, for I will appear in a cloud above the mercy seat.
Aaron shall enter the sanctuary with a bull from the herd as a sin offering and a ram as a burnt offering.

He shall put on a holy linen tunic and wear linen undergarments over his private parts, wrap a linen sash around his waist, and put a linen turban on his head, for these are holy garments. He shall wash his whole body with water and put them on.
From the congregation of the Israelites he shall take two male goats as a sin offering and one ram as a burnt offering.
Aaron shall present the bull for his own sins and make atonement for himself and for his household.
He shall take the two male goats and place them before the Lord at the entrance to the tent of the testimony.
Aaron shall cast lots over the two male goats, one lot for the Lord and one lot for release.
Aaron shall present the male goat on which the lot for release falls and place it alive before the Lord,
to make atonement with it, to send it away for release and let it go into the wilderness. The goat shall bear their lawless deeds upon itself into an untrodden place.
Aaron shall present his own bull as a sin offering and make atonement for himself and for his household, and he shall slaughter the bull that is his own sin offering.
He shall take a censer full of burning coals from the altar that is before the Lord, fill his hands with finely ground blended incense, and bring it behind the curtain.
He shall put the incense on the fire before the Lord, and the smoke of the incense shall cover the mercy seat that is above the testimony, so that he does not die.

He shall take some of the bull’s blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the east side of the mercy seat, and in front of the mercy seat he shall sprinkle some of that blood seven times with his finger.

He shall slaughter before the Lord the male goat that is the sin offering for the people, bring some of its blood behind the curtain, and do with its blood as he did with the bull’s blood. He shall sprinkle its blood on the altar before the mercy seat.

He shall make atonement for the sanctuary because of the impurities of the Israelites and their wrongdoings, for all their sins. He shall do the same for the tent of the testimony, which stands among them in the midst of their impurity.

No one at all shall be in the tent of the testimony when he enters to make atonement in the sanctuary, until he comes out. He shall make atonement for himself, for his household, and for the whole congregation of the Israelites.
He shall go out to the altar that is before the Lord and make atonement for it. He shall take some of the bull’s blood and some of the goat’s blood and put it on the horns all around the altar.
He shall sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, cleanse it, and sanctify it from the impurities of the Israelites.
He shall finish making atonement for the sanctuary, the tent of the testimony, and the altar, and perform purification for the priests. Then he shall present the live male goat.

Aaron shall lay his hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the lawless deeds of the Israelites, all their wrongdoings, and all their sins. He shall place them on the head of the live goat and send it into the wilderness through a man appointed for the task.
The goat shall bear their lawless deeds upon itself into an untrodden land, and he shall release the goat into the wilderness.
Aaron shall enter the tent of the testimony, take off the linen tunic that he wore when he entered the sanctuary, and leave it there.

He shall wash his body with water in the holy place, put on his robe, and go out and offer his burnt offering and the people's burnt offering. He shall make atonement for himself, for his household, and for the people, as for the priests.
They shall bring the fat of the sin offering up onto the altar.
The one who releases the goat designated for release shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterward he shall enter the camp.

They shall take outside the camp the bull for the sin offering and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought into the holy place to make atonement. They shall burn them with fire—their hides, their flesh, and their dung.
The one who burns them shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and afterward he shall enter the camp.
This shall be a lasting law for you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you shall humble yourselves and do no work, neither the native-born nor the foreigner residing among you.
For on that day atonement shall be made for you to cleanse you from all your sins before the Lord, and you shall be clean.
For it is a Sabbath of complete rest, and it shall be a day of rest for you. You shall humble yourselves, for this is a lasting law.
The priest who is anointed and whose hands are consecrated to serve as priest in his father's place shall make atonement. He shall put on the linen robe, a holy robe,
and he shall make atonement for the Holy of Holies, the tent of testimony, and the altar. He shall make atonement for the priests and for all the people.
This shall be a lasting law for you: to make atonement for the children of Israel for all their sins once a year. He shall do as the Lord commanded Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to Aaron, to his sons, and to all the children of Israel, and say to them:

This is what the Lord commanded, saying: Any man of the children of Israel who slaughters an ox, a sheep, or a goat in the camp, or who slaughters it outside the camp, and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of testimony to offer it as a burnt offering for well-being, acceptable to the Lord as a pleasing aroma, and whoever slaughters outside [?]

And if he does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of testimony to present an offering to the Lord before the Lord’s tent of testimony, bloodshed shall be charged to that man, as though he had shed blood. That person shall be cut off from his people.

so that the children of Israel may bring their sacrifices, which they themselves slaughter in the fields, and present them before the Lord at the entrance of the tent of testimony, to the priest, and slaughter them as sacrifices of well-being to the Lord.
The priest shall pour out the blood at the altar before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of testimony, and they shall offer up the fat as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
They shall no longer offer their sacrifices to the idols after which they prostituted themselves. This shall be a lasting law for you throughout your generations.
You shall say to them: Any man of the children of Israel, or of the foreigners residing among you, who offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice
and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of testimony to offer it to the Lord—that man shall be cut off from his people.
Any man of you children of Israel, or of the foreigners residing among you, who eats any blood—I will set my face against the person who eats blood and destroy him from among his people.
For the life of all flesh is its blood, and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your lives, for its blood makes atonement in place of its life.
Therefore I said to the children of Israel: No one among you shall eat blood, and the foreigner who has come to reside among you shall not eat blood.
Any man of the children of Israel, or of the foreigners residing among you, who hunts and catches an animal or a bird that may be eaten shall pour out its blood and cover it with earth.

For the life of all flesh is its blood, and I said to the children of Israel, “You shall not eat the blood of any flesh, for the life of all flesh is its blood. Anyone who eats it shall be destroyed.”

Every person who eats an animal that died on its own or was torn by wild beasts, whether a native inhabitant or a foreigner, shall wash their clothes and bathe their body. They shall be unclean until evening, and then they shall be clean.
But if they do not wash their clothes and do not bathe their body with water, they shall bear their guilt.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
He spoke to the children of Israel, and you shall say to them, “I am the Lord your God.”

You shall not follow any of the practices of the land of the Egyptians, where you lived as foreigners. You shall not follow the practices of the land of the Canaanites, to which I will bring you, and you shall not live according to their laws.
You shall carry out my judgments and keep my commandments, walking in them. I am the Lord your God.
You shall keep all my commands and all my ordinances and carry them out. Whoever carries them out shall live by them. I am the Lord your God.
No man shall approach any close relative of his own flesh to uncover their nakedness, for I am the Lord.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father or the nakedness of your mother, for she is your mother, and you shall not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s wife, for it is your father’s nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your sister, whether she is your father’s daughter or your mother’s daughter, whether born at home or elsewhere.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your son’s daughter or your daughter’s daughter. You shall not uncover their nakedness, for it is your own nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of the daughter of your father’s wife, for she is your sister who shares your father. You shall not uncover her nakedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s sister, for she is your father’s close relative.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother’s sister, for she is your mother’s close relative.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father’s brother, and you shall not have intercourse with his wife, for she is your relative.

You shall not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law, for she is your son’s wife. You shall not uncover her nakedness. And you shall not take her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter to uncover their nakedness, for they are your close relatives. It is wickedness.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother’s wife, for it is your brother’s nakedness.

You shall not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter. You shall not take her son’s daughter or her daughter’s daughter to uncover their nakedness, for they are your close relatives. It is wickedness.
You shall not take a woman together with her sister as a rival wife, uncovering her nakedness while her sister is alive.
You shall not have intercourse with a woman during the uncleanness of her menstrual period, uncovering her nakedness.
You shall not give your emission of semen to your neighbor’s wife, defiling yourself with her.
You shall not give any of your offspring to serve a ruler, and you shall not profane my holy name, for I am the Lord.
You shall not lie with a male as one lies with a woman, for that is an abomination.
You shall not release your semen into any animal, defiling yourself with it. No woman shall stand before any animal for it to mate with her, for that is detestable.
You shall not defile yourselves with any of these things, for the nations that I will drive out before you defiled themselves with all these things.
The land became loathsome, and I called it to account for its wrongdoing, and the land became sick of its inhabitants.
Keep my laws and all my commands, and do not commit any of these abominations, whether you are a native inhabitant, a newcomer, or a foreigner living among you.
For the people of the land who were there before you committed all these abominations, and the land became defiled.
So that the land does not also become sick of [?] when you defile it, as it became sick of the nations who were there before you.
For anyone who commits any of these abominations—the people who do them shall be cut off from among their people.
Keep my observances, so that you do not practice any of the abominable customs practiced before you, and do not defile yourselves by them, for I am the Lord your God.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the congregation of the children of Israel and say to them: Be holy, for I, the Lord your God, am holy.
Each of you shall revere your father and your mother, and keep my Sabbaths, for I am the Lord your God.
Do not follow idols, and do not make cast-metal gods for yourselves. I am the Lord your God.
If you offer a sacrifice of well-being to the Lord, offer it so that it may be accepted on your behalf.
It shall be eaten on the day you offer it and on the following day. If anything remains until the third day, it shall be burned with fire.
But if it is eaten on the third day, it is unfit as a sacrifice and shall not be accepted.
Whoever eats it shall bear sin, because he has defiled what is holy to the Lord. Those who eat it shall be cut off from their people.
When your reapers reap the harvests of your land, you shall not reap your fields completely by cutting close, and you shall not gather what has fallen from your harvest.
Do not glean your vineyard or gather its remaining grapes. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the Lord your God.
Do not steal, do not lie, and do not slander one another.
Do not swear falsely by my name, and do not profane the name of the Lord your God. I am the Lord your God.
Do not defraud your neighbor or rob him. Do not keep a hired worker’s wages with you overnight until morning.
Do not abuse a mute person, and do not put a stumbling block before a blind person. Fear the Lord your God. I am the Lord your God.
Do not act unjustly in judgment. Do not show favor to the poor or partiality to the rich. Judge your neighbor justly.
Do not go deceitfully among your people. Do not consent to the shedding of your neighbor’s blood. I am the Lord your God.
Do not hate your brother in your heart. You shall certainly rebuke your neighbor, and do not incur sin because of him.
Do not let your hand seek revenge, and do not bear a grudge against the children of your people. Love your neighbor as yourself, for I am the Lord.
Keep my laws. Do not breed your livestock with a different kind. Do not plant your vineyards with mixed varieties, and do not put on garments made of two kinds of material, which are abhorrent.
