If a man lies with a woman with an emission of semen, and she is a slave woman reserved for another man, but has not been redeemed by payment or granted her freedom, they shall be questioned and examined. They shall not be put to death, because she has not been freed.
He shall bring to the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of testimony, a ram as a guilt offering for his offenses.
The priest shall make atonement for him before the Lord with the ram of the guilt offering, for the sin he committed, and the sins he committed shall be forgiven him.

When you enter the land that the Lord God will give you and plant any tree bearing food, you shall cleanse it of its uncleanness. Its fruit shall be unclean for you for three years and shall not be eaten.
In the fourth year, all its fruit shall be holy, blessed to the Lord.
In the fifth year, you shall eat its fruit, so that its yield may increase for you. I am the Lord your God.
Do not eat on the mountains. Do not practice divination, consult birds for omens, or interpret bird omens.
Do not make tufts from the hair of your heads, and do not spoil the appearance of your beards.
Do not make cuts in your bodies for a dead person, and do not make incised markings on yourselves. I am the Lord your God.
Do not defile your daughter by making her a prostitute, lest the land become a prostitute and be filled with lawlessness.
Keep my Sabbaths and revere my holy places, for I am the Lord.
Do not follow mediums or turn to spiritists, defiling yourselves through them. I am the Lord your God.
Rise before the gray-haired, honor the elderly, and fear your God. I am the Lord your God.
If a foreigner settles among you in your land, do not oppress him.
The foreigner who has settled among you shall be to you like a native, and you shall love him as yourself, for you too were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
Do not act unjustly in judgment, in measuring, in weighing, or in using balances.
You shall have honest balances, honest weights, honest measures, and an honest dry measure. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
Keep all my laws and all my commandments, and carry them out, for I am the Lord God.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:

Speak to the children of Israel and say: If anyone among the children of Israel or among the foreigners residing in Israel gives his offspring to the ruler, he shall be put to death, and the people of the land shall stone him with stones.

I will set my face against that man and destroy him from among his people, because he gave some of his offspring to the ruler, defiling my sanctuary and making the name of those consecrated to me abominable.
But if the inhabitants of the land deliberately turn a blind eye to that man when he gives his offspring to the ruler, and do not kill him,
I will set my face against that man and his family, and I will destroy him and all who join him, whom he leads to prostitute themselves to the ruler, from among their people.
If anyone follows mediums or spiritists, prostituting himself by following them, I will set my face against that person and destroy him from among his people.
Sanctify yourselves and be holy, for I, the Lord your God, am holy.
Keep my commandments and carry them out. I am the Lord your God, who sanctifies you.
Any person who curses his father or his mother shall be put to death. If he reviles his father or his mother, he is liable to death.
If a man commits adultery with a married woman, or commits adultery with his neighbor’s wife, both the adulterer and the adulteress shall be put to death.
A man who sleeps with his father’s wife has exposed his father’s nakedness. Both shall be put to death, because they have acted wickedly and are liable to death.
If anyone sleeps with his daughter-in-law, both shall be put to death, because they have acted wickedly and are liable to death.
If a man sleeps with a male as with a woman, they have committed an abomination. Both shall be put to death, because they are liable to death.
If a man takes a woman and her mother, it is lawlessness. They shall burn him and the women with fire, so that there may be no lawlessness among you.
A man who has intercourse with an animal shall be put to death, and you shall kill the animal.
And if a woman approaches any animal to defile herself with it, you shall kill the woman and the animal. They shall be put to death, for they deserve death.

And if a man takes his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and sees her nakedness, and she sees his nakedness, it is a disgrace. They shall be cut off before the eyes of the children of their people, because he has uncovered his sister's nakedness. They shall bear their sins.
And if a man lies with a menstruating woman and uncovers her nakedness, he has uncovered the source of her blood, and she has uncovered the flow of her blood. Both shall be cut off from their people.
You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister or your mother's sister, for they have uncovered the nakedness of their own relatives. They shall bear their sins and die childless.
If a man sleeps with his uncle’s wife, he has uncovered his uncle’s nakedness. They shall bear their sins and die childless.
If a man takes his brother’s wife, it is an unclean act. He has uncovered his brother’s nakedness. They shall die childless.
You shall keep all my commands and all my ordinances and carry them out, and the land into which I bring you to live shall not be disgusted with [?].
You shall not follow the customs of the nations that I will drive out before you, for they did all these things, and I loathed them.
And I said to you, ‘You shall inherit that land, and I will give it to you as a possession, a land flowing with milk and honey.’ I am the Lord your God, who separated you from all the nations.

You shall distinguish for yourselves between clean and unclean animals and between clean and unclean birds. Do not defile yourselves with animals, birds, or any creatures that crawl on the earth, which I have set apart for you as unclean.
You shall be holy to me, for I, the Lord your God, am holy, and I have separated you from all the nations to be mine.
And a man or woman who is a medium or a diviner shall be put to death. You shall stone them with stones, for they deserve death.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said, ‘Speak to the sons of Aaron, the priests, and tell them not to defile themselves for the dead among their people,
or for a member of their household or for their neighbor, but for a father or mother, sons or daughters, or a brother,
or a sister or a daughter close to him who has not been given to a man in marriage. For these they may defile themselves.
They shall not defile themselves needlessly among their people, bringing defilement upon themselves.
They shall not shave their heads bald for the dead, nor shave the edges of their beards, nor make cuts in their bodies.
They shall be holy to their God and shall not profane the name of their God, for they offer the Lord's sacrifices, the offerings to their God, and they shall be holy.
They shall not marry a prostitute or a defiled woman, nor shall they marry a woman divorced from her husband, for the priest is holy to the Lord his God.
He shall sanctify himself, for he offers the offering of the Lord your God. He shall be holy, for I, the Lord who sanctifies them, am holy.
If the daughter of a priest defiles herself through prostitution, she has disgraced her father’s name. She shall be burned with fire.
The high priest among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil has been poured and whose hands have been consecrated to put on the robe, shall not uncover his head or tear his clothes.
He shall not go near a dead person. He shall not defile himself for his father or his mother.
He shall not leave the sanctuary or defile the sanctuary of his God, for the holy anointing oil from God is upon him. I am the Lord.
He shall marry a virgin from his own people.
He shall not marry a widow, a divorced woman, or a prostitute, but shall take a virgin from his own people as his wife.
He shall not defile his offspring among his people, for I am the Lord who sanctifies him.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to Aaron and say: Any man of your lineage, throughout all your generations, who has a defect shall not approach to present an offering to his God.
For no man who has a defect shall approach: a man who is lame or blind, has a shortened nose, or has a mutilated ear.
or a man with a broken hand or a broken foot,
or a hunchback, or someone cross-eyed or with an eye defect, or a man with scabies or cancer or only one testicle.
No man among the descendants of Aaron the priest who has a defect shall approach to present sacrifices to your God, because he has a defect. He shall not approach to present the offerings of God.
For the offerings of God are most holy; he may eat of the holy things.
But he must not approach the curtain or come near the altar, because he has a defect. He must not profane the holy place of his God, for I am the Lord who makes them holy.
And Moses spoke to Aaron, to his sons, and to all the Israelites.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Tell Aaron and his sons to be careful with the holy things of the Israelites, which they consecrate to me, and not to profane my holy name, for I am the Lord.

Tell them: Throughout your generations, any man among all your descendants who approaches the holy things that the Israelites consecrate to the Lord while he is unclean shall be cut off from my presence, for I am the Lord.

If any man among the descendants of Aaron the priest has leprosy or a discharge, he must not eat of the holy things until he becomes clean. The same applies to anyone who touches any uncleanness from a corpse, or a man who has a discharge of semen,
or anyone who touches any unclean creeping creature that makes people unclean, or a person who makes him unclean through any of that person's uncleanness.
The person who touches such a thing shall be unclean until evening and must not eat of the holy things unless he washes his body with water.
When the sun sets, he shall be clean, and afterward he may eat of the holy things, because they are his food.
He must not eat an animal that has died or has been torn by wild beasts, making himself unclean through them, for I am the Lord.
They must keep my requirements so that they do not incur sin because of them and die for profaning them, for I am the Lord who makes them holy.
No outsider may eat the holy things. A priest's guest and his hired worker must not eat of the holy things.
But if a priest buys a person with money, that person may eat of his food, and those born in his household may eat of his food.
If a priest's daughter marries an outsider, she must not eat of the produce of the holy things.
But if a priest's daughter becomes a widow or is divorced, has no children, and returns to her father's house as in her youth, she may eat of her father's food. No outsider may eat of it.
If a person unknowingly eats the holy things, he must add a fifth to their value and give the holy offering to the priest.
They must not profane the sacred portions of the Israelites' holy offerings, which they set apart for the Lord.
And they shall bring the guilt of transgression upon themselves by eating the most holy things, for I am the Lord who sanctifies them.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:

Speak to Aaron, to his sons, and to the whole congregation of the Israelites, and tell them: Any man of the Israelites, or of the resident foreigners who have joined them in Israel, who presents his offering in fulfillment of any of their vows or as any of their freewill offerings—whatever they present to the Lord as a burnt offering—to be acceptable from you,
it must be a male without defect, from the cattle, the sheep, or the goats.
They must not offer anything defective to the Lord, because it will not be acceptable from you.

Any man who presents his offering in fulfillment of any of their vows or as any of their freewill offerings, as a peace offering to the Lord, to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering or at your festivals, from the cattle or the sheep—it must be without defect to be acceptable. It must have no defect at all.

They must not offer to the Lord anything blind, lame, broken, with its tongue cut off, covered with warts, scabby, or afflicted with ringworm. You must not give any of these as a burnt offering on the Lord's altar.
You may slaughter for yourself an ox or a sheep with cropped ears or a docked tail, but they shall not be acceptable for your vows.
Do not offer to the Lord an animal whose testicles are [?], crushed, torn out, or cut off, and do not do this in your land.
Do not present any such animals as offerings to your God from the hand of a foreigner, because they have deformities and defects and will not be accepted from you.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
When a calf, a sheep, or a goat is born, it shall remain with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day onward it shall be acceptable as an offering presented to the Lord.
Do not slaughter cattle or sheep and their young on the same day.
When you sacrifice a thanksgiving sacrifice to the Lord, sacrifice it so that it may be accepted from you.
It shall be eaten that same day. Do not leave any of its meat until morning, for I am the Lord.
Keep my commandments and carry them out, for I am the Lord.
You shall not profane my holy name, for I am the Lord, and I shall be sanctified among the children of Israel. I am the Lord who sanctifies you,
who brought you out of the land of the Egyptians to be your God. I am the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: The festivals of the Lord, which you shall observe as holy assemblies—these shall be my festivals.
For six days you shall work, but on the seventh day there shall be a Sabbath of rest, designated as holy to the Lord. Do no work at all, for it is a Sabbath to the Lord wherever you live.
For these are the festivals of the Lord, designated as holy, which you shall proclaim at their appointed times.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, between the evenings, is the Lord’s Passover.
On the fifteenth day of that same month is the Lord’s Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
The first day shall be designated as holy for you. Do no ordinary work.
You shall present burnt offerings to the Lord for seven days. On the seventh day you shall have a holy assembly; you shall do no work of service.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: When you enter the land that I am giving you and reap its harvest, bring the sheaf, the first produce of your harvest, to the priest.
He shall lift up the sheaf before the Lord so that it may be accepted from you. The priest shall lift it up on the day after the first day.
On the day when he presents the sheaf, he shall offer an unblemished year-old lamb as a burnt offering to the Lord.
Its grain offering shall be two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering to the Lord as a pleasing aroma to the Lord. Its drink offering shall be a quarter of a hin of wine.
Do not eat bread or any roasted groats until the day when you present the offerings to your God. This is a perpetual statute throughout your generations, wherever you live.
Count for yourselves from the day after the Sabbath, from the day when you present the sheaf of the vow. Count seven complete weeks.
Count fifty days, up to the day after the last of the seven weeks, and present a new grain offering to the Lord.
From your dwellings you shall present two loaves as an offering. Each loaf shall be made from two tenths. They shall be baked with leaven as firstfruits for the Lord.

With the bread you shall present seven unblemished year-old lambs, one young bull from the herd, and two unblemished rams. They shall be a burnt offering to the Lord, together with their grain offerings and their drink offerings, an offering as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
You shall offer one male goat as a sin offering and two year-old lambs as a sacrifice of peace offerings, together with the bread of the firstfruits.

The priest shall present them as an offering before the Lord with the bread of the firstfruits, together with the two lambs. They shall be consecrated to the Lord and shall belong to the priest who presents them.
You shall proclaim that day as a designated holy assembly for yourselves. Do no ordinary work on it. This shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations, wherever you live.

When you reap the harvest of your land, do not gather in all the remnants of your field’s harvest as you reap, and do not collect what has fallen from your harvest. Leave it for the poor and the foreigner, for I am the Lord your God.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the Israelites and say: In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you shall have a day of rest, a memorial marked by trumpets, a holy assembly for the Lord.
Do not do any ordinary work, and offer a burnt offering to the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:

On the tenth day of the seventh month, which is the Day of Atonement, you shall have a holy assembly. Humble yourselves beginning on the evening of the ninth day, and offer burnt offerings to the Lord.
Do not do any work on that day, for it is the Day of Atonement, to make atonement for you before the Lord your God.
Anyone who does not humble himself on that day shall be destroyed from among his people.
Every person who does work on that day shall perish from among his people.
Do not do any work. This shall be a lasting ordinance throughout your generations, wherever you live.
It shall be a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you shall humble yourselves. From the evening of the ninth day of the month until the following evening, you shall observe your Sabbath.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the Israelites and say: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, the Feast of Booths shall be celebrated for the Lord for seven days.
The first day shall be a holy assembly. Do not do any ordinary work.

For seven days you shall offer burnt offerings to the Lord. On the seventh day you shall have a holy assembly and offer a burnt offering to the Lord, for this is the closing observance. Do not do any ordinary work.
These are the feasts of the Lord, which you shall proclaim as holy assemblies, to present gifts to the Lord: burnt offerings, their sacrifices, and offerings, day by day.
These are in addition to the Lord’s Sabbaths, your gifts, all your vowed offerings, and your freewill offerings that you give to the Lord.

On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the produce of the land, you shall celebrate a feast for the Lord for seven days. The first day shall be a day of rest, and the eighth day shall be a day of rest.
On the first day, take for yourselves fruit from beautiful trees, palm fronds, branches from leafy trees and willows, and branches of chaste trees from [?], to rejoice before the Lord for seven days.
You shall celebrate it as a feast for the Lord for seven days each year. This shall be a lasting ordinance throughout your generations. You shall celebrate it in the seventh month.
You shall live in booths for seven days. All the inhabitants of Israel shall live in booths.
So that your generations may know that I made the children of Israel live in booths when I brought them out of the land of the Egyptians. I am the Lord your God.
Moses told the Israelites about the feasts of the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Command the Israelites to bring you pure oil from olives picked while unripe, for lighting, so that a lamp may burn continually.

Outside the curtain, in the tent of testimony, Aaron and his sons shall keep it burning from evening until morning before the Lord without interruption. This shall be a lasting ordinance throughout your generations.
Burn the lamps on the holy lampstand before the Lord until morning.
You shall take fine flour and make it into twelve loaves. Each loaf shall be made from two-tenths.
You shall place them in two rows, six loaves in each row, on the holy table before the Lord.
You shall put pure frankincense and salt on the row, and they shall serve as a memorial for the bread, [?] to the Lord.
On the Sabbath day he shall set it before the Lord continually, as an everlasting covenant from the children of Israel.
It shall belong to Aaron and his sons, and they shall eat it in a holy place, for it is most holy for him among the offerings to the Lord, an everlasting ordinance.
The son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian man, went out among the Israelites. In the camp, the son of the Israelite woman fought with an Israelite man.
The son of the Israelite woman uttered the Name and cursed, and they brought him to Moses. His mother’s name was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
They placed him in custody so that he might be judged according to the Lord’s command.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Take the man who cursed outside the camp, and let those who heard him lay their hands on his head. Then let the whole congregation stone him.
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: Any man who curses God shall bear his sin.

For he has uttered the name of the Lord and shall be put to death. The whole congregation shall stone him with stones. Whether he is a foreigner or a native, he shall be killed for uttering the name of the Lord.
If a man strikes any human being and that person dies, he too shall be put to death.
Whoever strikes an animal shall make restitution, life for life.
If anyone maims his neighbor, what he has done shall likewise be done to him:
fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. Whatever injury someone inflicts shall likewise be repaid to him.
Whoever strikes a person and that person dies shall himself be put to death.
One and the same law shall apply to the foreigner and the native, for I am the Lord your God.
Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they took the man who had cursed outside the camp. The whole congregation stoned him with stones, and the Israelites did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai and said:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: When you enter the land that I will give you, the land that I give you shall rest, for it is a Sabbath to the Lord.
For six years you shall cultivate your field, and for six years you shall prune your vineyard and gather its fruit.
In the seventh year the land shall have a Sabbath of rest, for it is a Sabbath to the Lord. You shall not cultivate your field or prune your vineyard.
You shall not reap what grows by itself in your field, nor gather the grapes you have consecrated, for that is a year of rest for the land.
What your land produces during its Sabbath shall be food for you, your male servant, your female servant, your hired worker, and the foreigner staying with you.
All its produce shall also be food for your livestock and the wild animals in your land.
You shall count for yourself seven periods of rest, each lasting seven years—seven years seven times. These seven periods of seven years shall amount to forty-nine years.
You shall announce it with the sound of a trumpet throughout your land in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month. On the Day of Atonement you shall sound the trumpet throughout your land.

You shall consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim release throughout the land to all its inhabitants. That proclamation shall mark a year of release for you. Each person shall return to his property, and each person shall go back to his clan, for it is a proclamation of release.
The fiftieth year shall be a year for you [?]. You shall not sow, reap what grows by itself, or gather its consecrated grapes.
For it is a proclamation of release; it shall be holy to you. You shall eat its crops from the fields.
In the year of its proclamation of release, each person shall return to his property.
If anyone sells something to his neighbor or buys something from his neighbor, no one shall wrong his neighbor.
He shall buy from his neighbor according to the number of years after the jubilee; according to the number of years of harvests, he shall sell to you.

As the number of years increases, he shall increase his selling price, and as the number of years decreases, he shall reduce his selling price, for he sells to you according to the number of harvests.
No one shall wrong his neighbor, and you shall fear the Lord your God. I am the Lord your God.
You shall carry out all my ordinances and all my judgments, and you shall keep them and carry them out, and live securely in the land.
The land shall yield its produce, and you shall eat your fill and live in it safely.
But if you say, “What shall we eat in that seventh year, if we neither sow nor gather our crops?”
I will send my blessing upon you in the sixth year, and it shall yield enough produce for three years.
You shall sow in the eighth year and eat from the old produce until the ninth year. Until its harvest comes in, you shall eat from the old store.
The land shall not be sold permanently, because the land is mine, and you are strangers and sojourners before me.
Throughout all the land you possess, you shall allow the land to be redeemed.
If your brother who lives among you becomes poor and sells some of his property, his nearest relative shall come and redeem what his brother has sold.
But if someone has no relative to redeem it, and he becomes able to afford it and finds enough for its redemption,
he shall calculate the years since its sale and repay the balance to the man to whom he sold it, and return to his property.

But if he does not have enough to repay him, what he sold shall remain with the one who acquired it until the year of Jubilee. It shall be released in the year of Jubilee, and he shall return to his property.
If someone sells a dwelling house in a walled city, he shall have the right to redeem it until a year has passed from the day of its sale. His right of redemption shall last for that number of days.
But if it is not redeemed before a full year has passed, the house in the walled city shall belong permanently to its buyer and his descendants, and it shall not be released at the Jubilee.
But houses in villages that have no surrounding wall shall be reckoned as fields of the land. They shall always be subject to redemption, and they shall be released at the Jubilee.
In the cities of the Levites, the houses in the cities they possess shall always be subject to redemption by anyone among the Levites.

If anyone redeems property from the Levites, the houses sold in the cities they possess shall be released at the Jubilee, because the houses in the cities of the Levites are their possession among the children of Israel.
The fields set apart for their cities shall not be sold, because they are their permanent possession.
If your brother becomes poor and cannot support himself among you, you shall shelter him as a stranger and a sojourner, and your brother who is with you shall live.
Do not take usury or interest from him, and fear the Lord your God, for I am the Lord; and your brother shall live with you.
Do not lend him your money at interest, and do not give him your food for an increase.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of the Egyptians to give you the land of the Canaanites and to be your God.
If your brother becomes destitute among you and is sold to you, he shall not serve you as a slave.
He shall be with you as a hired worker and as a sojourner. He shall work for you until the year of Jubilee.
At the Jubilee he shall go free, he and his children with him, and he shall return to his family and go back to his ancestral property.
For they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of the Egyptians. They shall not be sold as slaves.
Do not oppress him with hard labor, and fear the Lord your God.
Whatever male or female slaves you may have, you shall acquire them from the nations around you.
You may also acquire slaves from the children of the foreigners who live among you, and from their relatives who are in your land; they shall become your property.
You shall pass them on to your children after you, and they shall be your slaves forever. But among your brothers, the children of Israel, none of you shall oppress his brother with hard labor.
If a newcomer or foreigner living among you prospers, and your impoverished brother sells himself to the newcomer or foreigner living among you, to a locally born offspring of the foreigner,
After his death, redemption shall be available to him. Any one of his brothers may redeem him.
His father's brother or his uncle's son may redeem him, or one of his blood relatives from his clan may redeem him. If he himself has the means, he may redeem himself.

He shall reckon with his purchaser from the year in which he was sold to him until the year of release. The money paid for him shall be reckoned as the wages of a hired worker, year by year, for as long as he is with him.
If he is to remain for more years than that, he shall pay his redemption price out of the money paid for his purchase.
And if only a few years remain until the year of release, he shall calculate for himself according to his remaining years and pay his redemption price.
He shall be like a hired worker, year by year, for as long as he is with him. His master shall not oppress him with hard labor in your sight.
If he is not redeemed in this way, he shall go free in the year of release, he and his children with him.
For the children of Israel are slaves belonging to me, my servants whom I brought out of the land of the Egyptians. I am the Lord your God.
Do not make handmade idols or carved images for yourselves. Do not erect a pillar for yourselves or place a stone monument in your land to bow down to it. I am the Lord your God.
Keep my Sabbaths and stand in awe of my holy places, for I am the Lord.
If you walk according to my decrees and keep my commandments and carry them out,
I will give you rain in its season, and the land shall yield its crops, and the trees of the fields shall yield their fruit.
Your threshing shall last until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest shall last until sowing. You shall eat your bread until you are satisfied and live securely in your land.
I will give peace in your land, and you shall sleep with no one to frighten you. I will destroy the harmful wild animals from your land, and war shall not pass through your land.
You shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall slain before you.
Five of you shall pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you shall pursue ten thousand. Your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.
I will look upon you, make you fruitful and multiply you, and establish my covenant with you.
You shall eat old produce, even produce stored for a very long time, and you shall clear away the old to make room for the new.
I will establish my covenant among you, and my soul shall not loathe you.
I will walk among you and be your God, and you shall be my people.
I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of the Egyptians when you were slaves. I broke the bonds of your yoke and led you out boldly.
But if you do not listen to me and do not carry out all these decrees of mine,
but rebel against them, and your souls become disgusted with my laws, so that you do not carry out all my commandments and break my covenant,

then I too will do this to you: I will bring upon you anxiety with distress, scabies and jaundice, which shall waste away your eyes, and you shall cry out in your souls. You shall sow your seed in vain, and your adversaries shall eat it.
I will set my face against you, and you will fall before your enemies. Those who hate you will pursue you, and you will flee even when no one is pursuing you.
And if you still do not listen to me, I will discipline you sevenfold for your sins.
I will break your arrogant pride, and I will make the sky above you like iron and your earth like bronze.
Your strength will be spent in vain. Your land will not yield its seed, and the trees of the fields will not yield their fruit.
And if you still walk perversely and refuse to listen to me, I will bring sevenfold more blows upon you according to your lawlessness.
I will send the savage beasts of the land against you, and they will devour you and destroy your livestock. I will make you few in number, and your roads will become impassable.
And if even by this you are not disciplined, but still walk perversely against me,
I too will act perversely against you in anger, and I will strike you sevenfold for your sins.
I will destroy you with the sword to exact vengeance for the covenant. And if you take refuge in your fortified cities, I will send pestilence among you, and you will be handed over to your enemies.
When you are afflicted with a shortage of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven and give you your bread by weight. You shall eat but not be satisfied.
And if even by this you do not listen to me, but walk perversely against me,
I too will act perversely against you in anger, and I will discipline you sevenfold according to your sins.
You will eat the flesh of your sons, and you will eat the flesh of your daughters.
I will tear down your pillars and destroy your wooden objects made by hand. I will cast your corpses upon the corpses of your idols, and I will abhor you.
I will make your cities ruins and leave your sanctuaries empty, and I will not smell the fragrance of your sacrifices.
I will lay your land waste, and your enemies who live in it will be astonished at it.
I will scatter you among the nations, and the sword coming against you shall destroy you. Your land shall be a wasteland, and your cities shall be empty.
Then the land will enjoy its sabbaths throughout all the days of its desolation, while you are in the land of your enemies, in a foreign land. Then the land will rest and enjoy its sabbaths.
Throughout all the days of its desolation, it will observe the sabbath rest that it did not observe during your sabbaths when you lived in it.

As for those of you who remain, I will bring trembling into their hearts in the land of their enemies. The sound of a rustling leaf will pursue them, and they will flee as people flee from battle. They will fall even when no one is pursuing them.
Each brother will abandon his brother as in battle, even when no one is pursuing them, and you will be unable to stand against your enemies.
You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will devour you.
Those of you who remain will perish because of their sins in the land of their enemies, and because of the sins of their fathers they will waste away with them.
They will confess their own sins and their fathers’ sins, because they transgressed and despised me, and because they walked perversely before me.
And I will walk in angry opposition to them and destroy them in the land of their enemies. Then their uncircumcised hearts shall be ashamed, and then they shall make amends for their sins.
And I will remember the covenant with Jacob, and the covenant with Isaac, and the covenant with Abraham; I will remember them, and I will remember the land.

The land will be abandoned by them. Then the land will receive its sabbaths while it lies desolate because of them, and they will bear the consequences of their lawlessness because they despised my judgments and abhorred my commandments.
And while they were in the land of their enemies, I did not disregard them or abhor them so as to destroy them and break my covenant with them, for I am the Lord their God.
And I will remember their former covenant, when I brought them out of the land of the Egyptians, out of the house of slavery, before all the nations, to be their God, for I am the Lord.
These are the judgments, commands, and laws that the Lord established between himself and the Israelites on Mount Sinai through Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the Israelites and say to them: Whoever makes a vow to give the value of his own person to the Lord,
the value of a male from twenty to sixty years old shall be fifty silver didrachms, according to the sanctuary shekel.
For a female, the value shall be thirty didrachms.
If the person is from five to twenty years old, the value of a male shall be twenty didrachms, and that of a female ten didrachms.
From one month to five years old, the value of a male shall be five silver didrachms, and that of a female three silver didrachms.
If the person is sixty years old or older, the value of a male shall be fifteen silver didrachms, and that of a female ten didrachms.

If he is too poor to pay the valuation, he shall stand before the priest, and the priest shall determine a value for him. The priest shall set his value according to what the person making the vow can afford.
If the offering is one of the animals that may be offered to the Lord, whatever he gives to the Lord from among them shall be holy.
He shall not exchange a good animal for a bad one, or a bad one for a good one. If he does exchange one animal for another, both the original animal and its replacement shall be holy.
If it is one of the unclean animals that may not be offered as an offering to the Lord, he shall present the animal before the priest.
The priest shall set its value, judging whether it is good or bad. Whatever value the priest sets for it shall stand.
If he redeems it, he shall add a fifth of its value to that amount.
If anyone dedicates his house as holy to the Lord, the priest shall set its value, judging whether it is good or bad. Whatever value the priest sets for it shall stand.
If the person who dedicated it redeems his house, he shall add a fifth of its value in silver to that amount, and it shall belong to him.
If anyone dedicates to the Lord some of the field belonging to his property, its value shall be according to the seed needed to sow it: fifty silver didrachms for one kor of [?].
If he dedicates his field in the year of release, its full assessed value shall stand.
If he dedicates his field after the year of release, the priest shall calculate the silver due according to the years remaining until the year of release, and shall deduct an amount from its value.
If the person who dedicated the field redeems it, he shall add a fifth of its value in silver to its assessed value, and it shall belong to him.
If he does not redeem his field and sells the field to another person, it shall no longer be redeemed.
When the field is released in the year of release, it shall be holy to the Lord, like land set apart, and shall become the priest’s property.
If he dedicates to the Lord a field that he purchased and that is not part of his own hereditary property,
the priest shall calculate its value for him up to the year of release, and he shall pay that value on that day as something holy to the Lord.
In the year of release, the field shall return to the man from whom it was purchased, whose own hereditary property the land was.
Every valuation shall be according to the sanctuary weights: twenty obols shall make one didrachm.
Every firstborn born among your livestock shall belong to the Lord, and no one shall consecrate it. Whether it is an ox or a sheep, it shall belong to the Lord.
If someone redeems one of the unclean animals, he shall add one-fifth to its assessed value, and it shall be his. But if it is not redeemed, it shall be sold at its assessed value.

Anything that anyone dedicates to the Lord from everything he owns, from a person to an animal and from a field to his possessions, shall not be returned or redeemed. Everything dedicated shall be most holy to the Lord.
No person devoted as an offering may be redeemed; that person must be put to death.
Every tithe of the land, whether from the seed of the land or from the fruit of the trees, belongs to the Lord; it is holy to the Lord.
If someone redeems his tithe, he shall add one-fifth to it, and it shall be his.
Every tithe of cattle and sheep, every tenth animal counted under the rod, shall be holy to the Lord.

There shall be no distinction between the good and the bad, and you shall not exchange the good for the bad. But if you do exchange it, both it and its replacement shall be holy, and it shall not be redeemed.
These are the commandments that the Lord commanded Moses for the children of Israel on Mount Sinai.
